# Chrome DevTools
Give your DeepSeek Harness Agent a real Chrome browser to drive and inspect.

This plugin installs Chrome DevTools MCP
as the Harness browser provider, so the Agent works a Chrom

e window you can
watch. It opens pages, reads them, clicks and types, takes screenshots, reads
conso

le messages and network requests, runs scripts, records performance traces,
and runs Lighthouse audi

messages and network requests, runs scripts, records performance traces,
and runs Lighthouse audits.

Chrome belongs to the chat that opened it. Close the chat and its browser goes
with it, so one conve
rsation can never drive another one's pages.
## What you can ask for

- *"Open example.com, screenshot it, and tell me the console errors."*
- *"Go to my app on localhost

:3000, sign up with a test account, and tell me
whether the confirmation step works."*
- *"Record a

performance trace on localhost:3000 and explain the largest
contentful paint."*
- *"Run a Lighthouse

audit on localhost:3000 and tell me what fails
accessibility."*
- *"Screenshot that page at 375 pix

els wide so I can check the mobile layout."*
- *"Click the thing that is broken and tell me exactly

what the network request
returns."*
## Install

1. In the Harness, open **Plugins** in the left sidebar.
2. Press **Install**.
3. Paste this reposit

ess, open **Plugins** in the left sidebar.
2. Press **Install**.
3. Paste this repository's address:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

4. Install it, then refresh the page.
5. **Start a new chat.** The Agent connects a browser when a c

hat begins, so a
chat that was already open when you installed keeps running without one.

The install dialog accepts a GitHub address, a package name, or a local folder.
To pin the release t

his README describes, paste
`github:DevTarlow/dsh-chrome-devtools#v0.1.0` instead. If you would rath

er ask
your Agent, say: *"Install the bundle `github:DevTarlow/dsh-chrome-devtools`."*

You need Google Chrome (or Chrome for Testing) at its current stable version.
The plugin finds it by

itself, so a normal installation needs no configuration.
You also need a desktop session, because t
he browser opens a real window.
## Check it works
In a new chat, ask:
> Open example.com and tell me its title and any console errors.

A Chrome window opens, loads the page, and the Agent answers from what it read.
If you would rather
not open a window, see `headless` under Settings.
## Settings

The plugin's defaults are set in cordis.patch.yml. To change
one, put the same override in your own

Harness profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — for
example `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` — then sta

e's `cordis.patch.yml` — for
example `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` — then start a new chat.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Any setting you leave out falls back to the plugin's own default rather than this
bundle's, so resta
te every value you still want whenever you edit that block.
| Setting | Default | What it does |
| `mode` | `launch` | `launch` starts a fresh Chrome for each chat. Use `attach` to drive a browser

you started yourself. |
| `headless` | `false` | `false` opens a window you can watch. Set `true` on

a server or in CI, where there is no display. |
| `executablePath` | unset | Which Chrome to launch
. Left unset, the plugin finds it. Set it for an unusual install, or for the wrapper in Common quest

ions. |
| `endpoint` | — | Required by `attach`: the debugging address of the browser you started, s

uch as `http://127.0.0.1:9222`. |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | the client's own | How long one tool call
may take, in milliseconds. |
### Drive your own browser instead

`launch` gives every chat a fresh profile, which means it starts logged out. To
keep the tabs, cooki

es and logins you already have, start Chrome yourself and
point the plugin at it.

and leaves your br

that browser at a time. When the chat ends, the plugin disconnects
and leaves your browser running.

Start that browser before you open a chat. The plugin connects when a chat is
created, so a chat sta
rted while the browser is unreachable has no browser tools.
## Chrome extensions

The browser this plugin launches is a clean, isolated profile with extensions
disabled, so it cannot

load or test an unpacked extension. To test one, attach
the plugin to a Chrome you start yourself,
with the extension already loaded:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin then drives the pages with its normal browser tools. It does not pass
Chrome DevTools MCP

's `--category-extensions` flag, so the extension-specific
tools (`install_extension`, `reload_exten

sion`, `list_extensions`,
`trigger_extension_action`) and `chrome-extension://` pages are not availa

ble
through the plugin. Use the `chrome-devtools` CLI from the same pinned
`chrome-devtools-mcp` rel

plugin. Use the `chrome-devtools` CLI from the same pinned
`chrome-devtools-mcp` release for those:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Loading an extension over a browser URL needs Chrome 149 or newer. Stop the CLI
daemon with `chrome-
devtools stop` when you are done.

Use a dedicated profile for that browser. The debugging port gives anything on
the machine full cont

rol of it, so keep it bound to localhost and stop the
browser when you finish testing.
### Use your existing logged-in Chrome

Chrome 136+ does not allow `--remote-debugging-port` against the default profile,
but you can let th

e CLI attach to the Chrome you are already using. Enable
Chrome's remote debugging bridge (Chrome 14

1. Open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` in that Chrome.
2. Turn on **Enable remote debugging**

and leave the browser running.
3. Click **Allow** when Chrome asks to allow the session.
